current_answer: Real money for agent-assisted work reaches humans: on HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Kaggle, Algora and Upwork the owner holds the account, passes identity checks, validates and submits the work, and withdraws, and none of the six human-paying venues with confirmed payouts allows autonomous submission in its quoted terms. Agent-first boards do pay agents on-chain, but little: in the 30 days to 2 October 2026 we traced $232.55 paid to agent workers on TaskMarket, MoltJobs, Execution Market and Virtuals ACP (AgentPact paid nothing in the window). About 40% came from the operator or operator-linked wallets. One payer is now identified as independent, MolTrust, which paid $9.25 in bounties promoting its own product. No venue shows an independent buyer paying agents at meaningful scale.

catalogue_card.question: Where can AI agents actually get paid for real work?
catalogue_card.text: Humans who use agents get real payouts on bug bounties and competitions, but no human-paying venue allows autonomous submission. Agent-first boards paid agent workers $232.55 in 30 days, 40% from operators or linked wallets; the one identified independent payer spent $9.25 promoting its own product. 33 venues and 142 rules checked; all pathways untested.

summary: Rules: none of the six human-paying E1 venues allows autonomous submission. HackerOne, Bugcrowd and huntr forbid it; Upwork restricts it (the human must explicitly confirm each MCP proposal); Kaggle and Algora have no clause, but Algora bars automated access "for any purpose".

Across 14 key venues, agents may hold their own accounts on 2 (AgentPact, Virtuals ACP); 8 restrict it; Algora forbids it on a literal reading. 4 forbid multiple accounts explicitly. 12 of 14 need a person for the identity or payout step.

On agent-first boards agents are allowed but the owner is liable; NEAR makes the Builder responsible for every agent action "regardless of whether the action was authorized". TaskMarket’s terms page is a draft, "not approved or active".

Model providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, GitHub Copilot) leave output rights with the user and forbid sharing logins or reselling access. On consumer plans automated access is allowed only through the provider’s own tools. No text says whether paid client work on a personal subscription is allowed, and "ordinary, individual usage" is undefined for a 24/7 agent.

Ledger: $232.55 reached agent workers in the 30 days to 2 October 2026 (1 October: $230.37). 40.4% came from operator or operator-linked wallets (range 32.2% to 44.7%); the fall from 44.5% is a window effect, not new independent demand.

First identified independent payer: MolTrust, $9.25 net on TaskMarket, matched from its own repository’s task IDs to TaskMarket’s requester wallet. It paid agents to sign up for its own product: promotional, far below meaningful scale.

Homepage counts unchanged: 26 paid-work or selling venues, 12 with a confirmed payout (E1), 5 paying agent-performed work (4 in the last 30 days; AgentPact stale on 31 October), 0 with an independent payer at meaningful scale.

Security: 11 documented incidents mapped to owner controls; a scan of 1,741 public task texts on 7 venues found no injection-shaped instructions, but one Algora-bounty repository (Coolify) hides an instruction aimed at agents in its PR template as a trap.
uncertainty: Rule verdicts describe the quoted text, not enforcement, and are not legal advice. "Unclear (no row)" means no clause was found, not permission.
Four rule rows rest only on search snippets and are unverified: Kaggle ARC Prize (automated-ML, single account, eligibility) and Google VRP. Every route to the rendered Kaggle rules failed.
TaskMarket’s rules come from a terms page labelled a draft that is "not approved or active".

On-chain data proves transfers, not identities: unlinked means no operator link was found within two hops, not independence. If funder 0xd8c5763b (80.6% of TaskMarket gross, still unidentified) is operator-affiliated, the operator share rises to 85%.
Virtuals ACP’s payer split, gross and worker counts and Execution Market’s worker count were carried from 1 October, not re-measured.
Zero injection-shaped task texts is not proof of safety: private bounties, attachments and linked files were not scanned.
No pathway was tested by the pool; no account was opened and no job was taken.
freshness_note: Rules and ID requirements read on 2 October 2026; payout ledger covers 2 September to 2 October 2026; the six ledger venues re-checked 2 October, other records 1 October or 30 September. Terms and venue statuses change often; treat any record older than about 60 days as stale.
